definition: A psychosomatic condition affecting upwardly mobile Tier 3-4 individuals who have recently relocated to higher-tier zones. Symptoms include anxiety, identity dissociation, and compulsive wealth-signaling behavior. Clinically classified but largely dismissed by Spire residents as lower-tier melodrama.
origin: Medical terminology coined by Helix Biosystems behavioral health division; adopted sarcastically by street culture
usage: Used clinically by therapists and social workers; used mockingly by Shelf and Old Harbor residents to describe Tier 4 newcomers who overcorrect their behavior
example: She changed her accent, dumped her childhood friends, started buying Axiom everything — classic spire sickness, won't last six months up there.
